core.text: Necessity-account successful future, hypothetical: immutable-key selection plus refresh before each commit produces only K2/K5/K7 checked and final S2 within ten minutes. Backcast through commits ending at 3, 6 and 9 to selects ending at 1, 4 and 7 and refreshes ending at 2, 5 and 8; final refresh ends at 10. Key binding must preserve intended identity through the first refresh. This success would establish compatibility with intermediate refreshes, not their necessity.

Selection-reordering-account successful future, hypothetical: row-bound S0 selection/commit pairs ending at 2, 4 and 6 write K2/K5/K7; refresh ending at 7 loads S2 with statuses preserved by key. Backcast from final freshness to the last commit and then to an unchanged loaded order during every selection/commit interval. The first divergence from the preferred select-refresh-commit path is committing during 1-2 instead of refreshing; snapshot eligibility alone does not change loaded order.

Preserve a separating 2x2 replay: intermediate refresh versus final-only refresh, crossed with row versus immutable-key binding. All arms select during 0-1, 3-4 and 6-7; commit during 2-3, 5-6 and 8-9; refresh finally during 9-10. At 1-2, 4-5 and 7-8, final-only arms inspect the same retained target instead of refreshing, matching elapsed time. Record the first divergence at minute 2: loaded order and retained target identity, then actual written key at minute 3. Score every write and final status, not merely repaired final correctness.

residue.text: The equal score 75 cannot distinguish K5 from K7. Verify immutable keys throughout and after final S2 refresh. Neither rival may count score agreement alone as successful target identification.

Only one synthetic miswrite is stipulated. Neither successful future nor repeated mismatch-refresh feedback has been observed. Log mismatch requests separately if tested; production binding, human detection costs, concurrency and load failures remain unresolved. These probes support claims only about the eight-record model.

tension.account_a: Necessity hypothesis: reliable correction requires intermediate refresh before every commit, even when key identity is preserved.
tension.account_b: Selection-reordering hypothesis: refresh-induced row identity changes cause miswrites; intermediate refresh is unnecessary for fixed-key targets.
tension.prediction_a: Both final-only arms fail reliable completion despite final S2 freshness; a successful final-only replay falsifies necessity within this model.
tension.prediction_b: Only intermediate-refresh plus row-binding miswrites: its first commit writes K5 instead of K2. Both final-only arms and intermediate-refresh plus key-binding succeed, prospectively, within ten minutes.
